ideas.name: DriftLock
ideas.niche: AR spatial stability and environmental anchor mapping for digital street artists.
ideas.problem: Spatial drift and the inability to precisely pin complex digital assets to irregular, non-flat, or high-texture urban surfaces under shifting lighting conditions.
ideas.targetUser: Digital muralists, AR installation designers, and urban media artists (ages 20-40) who create site-specific augmented reality content for city environments.
coreFeatures: Micro-Anchor Isolation: High-contrast detection of physical 'fiducials' like cracks, grout lines, and texture edges to serve as high-precision anchor points.
LumenSync Metadata: Captures ambient light intensity, color temperature, and shadow vectors to allow artists to match digital lighting to the physical environment.
Mesh-to-Coordinate Export: Generates standardized JSON/XML data containing spatial anchor coordinates and depth-map slices for seamless import into Unity, Unreal, or Blender.
Drift Simulation Preview: A diagnostic tool that visualizes potential spatial drift based on the detected texture density of a surface.
realDependencies: ARKit/ARCore (for SLAM and spatial tracking)
LiDAR/Depth API (for high-fidelity surface geometry)
OpenCV (for advanced edge and feature detection)
Cloud Spatial Anchors (for persistent, multi-user environmental persistence)
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will bypass real-time sensor data by using a pre-recorded 4K video of a textured urban wall as the 'live camera feed.' To simulate LiDAR, a post-processing shader will overlay a pseudo-depth mesh onto the video. The 'Micro-Anchor Detection' will be simulated by triggering hardcoded coordinate pop-ups at specific timestamps in the video loop. A simulated processing delay (2-3 seconds) with a 'Scanning Environment...' progress bar will be used to mimic the computational load of OpenCV, and the 'Export' function will generate a static, mock JSON file containing pre-written coordinate arrays.

ideas.name: ChromaGrain
ideas.problem: The 'Digital Flattening' effect, where the physical nuance of brushstrokes, impasto textures, and organic color gradients is lost or distorted during the scanning-to-software transition due to improper DPI, color profiles, and bit-depth settings.
ideas.targetUser: Professional fine artists (oil, acrylic, watercolor) and concept artists who utilize traditional media as a foundation for digital painting and post-production workflows.
coreFeatures: Reference Swatch Calibration: Uses a physical color checker card in the scan to generate custom ICC profiles for perfect chromatic accuracy.
Texture Depth Profiler: Analyzes micro-contrast and shadows in a scan to recommend optimal bit-depth and DPI settings for preserving physical paint volume.
Medium-Specific Presets: One-tap configuration profiles for specific media (e.g., 'Heavy Impasto Oil', 'Wet-on-Wet Watercolor', 'Charcoal Grain').
Layered Texture Extractor: Generates high-resolution texture maps from scans to be used as digital overlay layers in Photoshop or Procreate.
realDependencies: TWAIN/WIA Scanner Driver APIs
LittleCMS or Adobe Color Engine for ICC profile generation
OpenCV for computational texture and edge analysis
Cloud-based Profile Sync (AWS S3/DynamoDB)
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will bypass hardware drivers by using a 'Simulated Scanner' file upload component that triggers a 5-8 second progress bar with randomized 'calibration' status messages. Instead of real-time image processing, the app will use a local library of pre-processed 'Before' and 'After' image pairs; when a user selects a specific medium preset, the app will display the corresponding 'After' image and mapped metadata (DPI/Color Profile) as if it were calculated on the fly. All 'Analysis' graphs will be hardcoded UI elements that populate after a simulated processing delay to mimic high-compute texture analysis.

ideas.name: LumenRef
ideas.niche: Real-world light-to-material interaction documentation for CGI
ideas.problem: Digital artists struggle to accurately replicate how specific light temperatures (Kelvin) and intensities (Lux) affect complex physical properties like anisotropy, subsurface scattering, and micro-surface roughness, leading to 'unnatural' looking digital renders.
ideas.targetUser: Professional VFX Lighting Artists, 3D Texture Artists, and Architectural Visualizers working in high-end film, game development, or product rendering pipelines.
coreFeatures: Multi-Parametric Observation Logger (Captures Kelvin, Lux, Incident Angle, and Material Type)
Searchable Spectral Material Library (Filterable by material class and light condition)
PBR Value Suggestion Engine (Maps real-world data to Roughness, Metallic, and Specular values)
Visual Comparison Mode (Side-by-side view of real-world photo vs. simulated shader preview)
realDependencies: AWS S3 for high-resolution image and metadata hosting
Google Vision API for automated material classification from uploads
PostgreSQL for complex relational querying of material properties
Bluetooth API for integration with handheld spectrophotometer hardware
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will use a local 'mock_library.json' containing 30 pre-defined material-light interaction profiles. Image 'uploads' will be intercepted by a mock service that triggers a 2-second 'Processing...' loading state before returning a static Unsplash URL. The PBR Suggestion Engine will utilize a simple coefficient-based lookup table (mapping input Kelvin/Lux to static Roughness/Metallic values) instead of a real physics engine. All search and filter requests will implement a 500ms artificial delay to simulate database latency.

ideas.name: SonicStitch
ideas.problem: The communication gap between wardrobe departments and sound designers, causing a mismatch between the visual material of a costume and its acoustic presence in post-production.
ideas.targetUser: Sound designers, Foley artists, and Costume Supervisors working in film, high-end commercial production, and AAA video game development.
coreFeatures: Material Acoustic Profiler: A library mapping textile types (e.g., heavy denim, silk, waxed canvas) to frequency ranges and transient characteristics.
Layered Wardrobe Builder: A tool to stack clothing items (base layer, mid-layer, outer layer) to visualize the additive sonic profile of a full outfit.
Movement-Texture Timeline: A visual sequencer to map character actions (running, crouching, combat) against specific wardrobe layers to predict foley intensity.
Foley Session Export: Automated generation of technical shot lists for foley artists, detailing required materials and movement intensities per scene.
realDependencies: High-fidelity audio sample library (AWS S3)
Real-time Digital Signal Processing (DSP) engine for acoustic layering
Real-time collaborative database for production teams (Supabase or Firebase)
Advanced spectral analysis API for material-sound matching
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will use a 'MockDSP' service that returns pre-recorded loops of specific textures (e.g., 'silk_rustle.wav', 'leather_creak.wav') instead of real-time synthesis. To simulate cloud latency, all data fetches will be wrapped in an async function with a randomized 400ms to 1200ms delay using setTimeout. The Layering Simulator will fake additive complexity by simply increasing the gain/volume of overlapping mock audio tracks. The 'Material Profiler' will display static, pre-rendered frequency graphs stored in a local JSON object rather than performing live FFT analysis.

ideas.name: Pivotly
ideas.niche: Creative decision-log and rationale tracker for small design teams.
ideas.problem: Circular debates and 'creative looping' where teams revisit and re-litigate previously rejected design directions, leading to decision fatigue and wasted production hours.
ideas.targetUser: Creative Directors and Lead Designers at boutique creative agencies (3-15 employees) managing high-iteration client projects and multiple stakeholders.
coreFeatures: Pivot Journaling (Mandatory 'Why' documentation for every aesthetic or structural shift)
Decision Audit Timeline (A visual history showing the evolution of project logic)
Loop-Back Flagging (A search/filter tool to quickly compare new suggestions against previously rejected rationales)
Stakeholder Lock-in (A lightweight sign-off mechanism to formalize and 'freeze' a chosen direction)
realDependencies: Firebase Auth or Auth0 for user identity and team permissions
Supabase or PostgreSQL for relational storage of decision logs and links
AWS S3 or Cloudinary for hosting visual reference assets and moodboards
Socket.io or Ably for real-time collaborative updates during live meetings
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will utilize a 'MockDataService' class that wraps all data requests in async functions with a random delay of 500ms to 1500ms to simulate network latency. Authentication will be simulated by checking a 'demo_user' key in localStorage, bypassing actual OAuth with a 1-second 'verifying credentials' loading state. The database will be a large, pre-defined JSON object containing nested project, pivot, and user arrays. For image assets, the app will use Unsplash source URLs with specific keywords (e.g., 'minimalist-design') to simulate a real design library. Real-time collaboration will be emulated by a setInterval loop that randomly triggers 'User is typing...' or 'User updated a pivot' toast notifications to simulate active team presence.
